title: MATURATION OF ZERO BOIL OFF COMPONENTS (RTB CRYOCOOLER) OF LIQUID OXYGEN (LOX) - EXPRO+
description: Objective:  To design and develop a cryocooler breadboard model, based on the Reverse Turbo-Brayton, targeting LOx temperature, for the long duration storage of liquid cryogenic propellants for in Space application. Description:  Cryogenic propellants are being considered and baselined for future missions as a valid alternative to storable propellants for orbital and deep space missions.A combination of Liquid Oxygen (LOX) and Liquid cryogenic propellants provide significant advantages in term of performance over storable fuel and oxidizers.  Several classes of orbital and deep space missions can benefit from cryogenic propulsion systems. However, cryogenic propulsion systems technologies are only available for short duration missions (max. 1 day, launchers). Extending the operating life of these systems requires a range of new technologies, more adapted to high volume transfer at lower pressure, andfor a long-time duration of operations and long cycles in space (days to weeks).  Handling cryogenic fluid in space for long duration necessitates the introduction of a so called Zero Boil off systems where active cooling systems are needed.  In order to increase TRL for such system and especially for the cryocooler part, this activity targets to design, manufacture a testing model and perform test under representative environment on ground, targeting the LOx temperature range, of around 90K, coinciding also with sub-cooled LCH4, and would also demonstrate the first technological bricks for a LH2 RTB cryocooler of such size. Also the heat lifts is targeted to be in the range of 100-200W, which is considered an important stepping stone into enabling zero boil-off components storage in-orbit of cryogenic propellants.   This activity encompasses the following tasks:   - - - - Requirements definition, design trade-offs, a development plan, industrial plan (incl. make or buy analyses) to reach TRL4 at the end of the activity at component level, A systems sizing exercise (considering ZBO LOX tank application), and the associated detailed design of the 90K Class RTB Breadboard Test plan, HW manufacturing and testing Test results exploitation, lessons learned and recommendations for future or complementary development Deliverables: Breadboard, Report

title: SUSTAINABLE 3D-PRINTED ACTIVE AND PASSIVE RF COMPONENTS FOR ANTENNA ARRAY APPLICATIONS - EXPRO+
description: Objective:To develop and demonstrate 3D-printed active and passive RF components for L-band antenna arrayapplications, enabling more sustainable manufacturing and system integration.Description:The environmental impact of space activities is receiving increasing attention across the European spacesector. In line with ESA's Ecodesign Policy, future missions are expected to assess their environmentalfootprint through Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) and identify and implement solutions that reduce resourceconsumption, energy usage, waste generation, and hazardous materials. RF hardware is a particularly relevant target for ecodesign improvements due to its widespread deployment across satellite payloads and user terminals. Given the large number of RF components typically integrated within phased-array antenna architectures, even incremental reductions in environmental impacts at component level can translate into significant cumulative benefits at system and programme level.Phased Array Antennas (PAAs) are a key enabling technology for next-generation communications,navigation, and sensing systems, providing electronically steerable beams, enhanced reliability, andoperational flexibility. Conventional PAA manufacturing relies on complex and resource-intensive productionprocesses. Additive manufacturing, and in particular 3D printing, offers a sustainable alternative approachthrough the use of functional polymers and carbon-nanotube-based materials while reducing waste, energyusage, water consumption, and chemical processing.While significant progress has been achieved for passive RF components, the development of active RFdevices, particularly RF transistors, remains a key challenge and a barrier to fully 3D-printed RF systems. The ESA Discovery activity "GHz Organic Printed Transistors" (GHioza) demonstrated sustainable 3D-printed transistor technology up to approximately 300 MHz which is state of the art but not sufficient for phase-array antenna applications. The activity aims to develop sustainably manufactured 3D-printed RF transistorsoperating in L-band (1-2 GHz) and integrate them with antenna elements on a common substrate,demonstrating the co-integration of active and passive RF functionality within a unified additively manufacturedplatform. A proof-of-concept active array demonstrator comprising two to three antenna elements andassociated active circuitry will then be developed, with electronic beam steering demonstrated using anexternal Software Defined Radio for beamforming and phase control.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- requirements analysis- material characterization- RF transistor design- antenna/component co-integration- additive manufacturing process development- prototype fabrication- RF testing and validation- beam-steering demonstrations- development plan- Simplified LCA analysis and Ecodesign trade off and selection.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). title: ORGANIC MATERIALS USED IN LAUNCHERS APPLICATIONS - EXPRO+
description: Objective:To establish a de-risking strategy for the non-European dependency for organic materials such as silicones,elastomers, glues, resins for thermal protections for launchers applications.Description:In 2025, European chemistry faces critical challenges due to structural crises, industrial site closures, andintense international competition. Many groups in Europe and outside of Europe are reorganizing theirproduction, closing plants, or relocating to more competitive regions like Asia. Between 2019 and 2023,Europe's chemical production fell by 12%, with closure of over 20 industrial sites. In addition, groups must faceevolutions of regulations (e.g. REACH), monitoring and anticipating future forbidden substances (Substancesof Very High Concern - SVHC) and focus newinvestments on green chemistry and decarbonization viabiosourced molecules, recycling, and carbon capture. For example, PFAS regulation will be effective at leastby end of 2028, and a huge number of products will be forbidden, and aeronautic and aerospace sectors willbe severely impacted. For silicones some non-European suppliers informed that a supply risk exists for someolder references.The qualification of these applications is long and complex. Silicones are used in componentsin the manufacture of thermal protection to contribute for maintaining the shape and the flexibility of the thermalprotection. title: SUPPORT TO THE STANDARDISATION OF THE SATELLITE 6G COMPONENT (ARTES FP 1D.029) EXPRO+
description: The purpose of the activity is to coordinate satcom sector involvement in the 6G standardisation process of the 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP). The activity scope includes building consensus amongst satcom players, developing contributions to support standardisation actions, and advocating positions favourable to the sector within the standardisation process. The overarching goal being to ensure that the standardisation process results in tangible new opportunities for the satcom industry. In particular, the activity will include support to the Non-Terrestrial Network (NTN)-related work items defined for Release 21 of the 3GPP specification, as well as the preparation of NTN-related items for Release 22 and beyond.
